rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: BKCB2 recommends increased funding for B-HEARD multi-agency response teams deployed for non-emergency calls. The Behavioral Health Emergency Assistance Response Division (B-HEARD) is limited in its hours of operation, its geographic distribution, and in the types of calls considered eligible for a response. This means that many people who may need a B-HEARD team are instead provided a "traditional response" by the NYPD. B-HEARD currently covers only 31 of the 79 NYPD Precincts. BKCB2 requests expansion of the B-HEARD program to the 84th and 88th Precincts within BKCD2.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: Due to the ongoing expansion of large housing developments in the district, the population and increase in family size is evident. We are in need of a new hospital based in the district to provide the necessary medical needs of existing and new residents. RESPONSE TO AGENCY: CB5 is resubmitting this request to emphasize the obvious need to conduct a study to assess the need based on existing & historic health concerns and time frame since a public hospital has existed in the district.
rows.headline: Provide a new or expanded health care facility
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency does not support and cannot accommodate Explanation: NYC Health + Hospitals is currently in the process of modernizing its infrastructure, increasing its capacity and expanding the range of services it offers to better respond to the community’s growing healthcare needs. In order to create a new health care facility, H+H needs to closely coordinate with the State and conduct a community needs assessments to determine its viability. If the results of the assessment are positive, NYC Health + Hospitals will need to create a master plan and seek capital funding. Please note that the cost and effort required to construct a new facility is significant and NYC Health + Hospitals is currently unable to undertake a project of this magnitude due to lack of funding. "

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: Funds are requested for the opening of a more permanent indoor Red Hook COVID testing and vaccination location. This could be resolved be reopening the H+H location at Red Hook Recreation Center. While we hope COVID-19 will continue to decrease, variants and waves show that flexibility is essential in order to reach high-need areas as surges happen and positivity rates change. The existing mobile vans are often absent or out of commission and there is no way to schedule a test nor call the van to check if it is there on a given day. For residents with disabilities, that means a potentially perilous walk in the cold or snow to see whether the van there. CB6 does not have an H+H facility and thus lacks access to rapid point-of-care testing.
rows.headline: Provide a new or expanded health care facility
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency does not support and cannot accommodate Explanation: NYC Health + Hospitals transitioned the NYC Test & Treat Corps in May 2023 as a result of the expiration of the Federal COVID-19 Public Health Emergency declaration. These services transitioned to more permanent services inside the public health care system’s hospitals and community-based outpatient care centers , including in NYC Health + Hospital’s COVID-19 Centers of Excellence (COE). There are three locations, with one located in Brooklyn. The COE provides short- and long-term follow-up care for those recovering from COVID-19. It also offers primary care services to help you manage all health conditions and offers self management tools for chronic diseases. Rapid testing is also available outside of NYC Health + Hospitals facilities, such as at local pharmacies.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: This city hospital is a staple. It needs to be modernize to keep pace with population growth and demand.
rows.headline: Renovate or upgrade an existing health care facility
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency supports but cannot accommodate Explanation: H+H recognizes there are many unfunded capital needs across the system, including at Kings County Hospital. While not all of these needs can be accommodated with the limited financial resources, H+H has allocated some capital funding to address the modernization needs at Kings County, including clinical renovations such as expanding the Emergency Department and the CT suite, renovation of the Labor & Delivery space, and the conversion of cath labs to operating rooms; upgrades of building infrastructure such as roof replacements at multiple buildings on the campus, rehabilitating the steam tunnel, and electrical upgrades. Many of these projects are currently underway but given the scale of the upgrades - these are multi-million dollar upgrades, it will take a few years before the projects are complete. H+H will continue to seek capital funding from various stakeholders to address the needs at Kings County.

rows.claim: Published request and agency response; not an appropriation or solicitation.
rows.explanation: A Level 1 Trauma Center is urgently needed at South Brooklyn Health (formerly Coney Island Hospital). With the rapidly increasing population from new housing developments, along with the influx of tourists during the summer season, the demand for immediate, high-level emergency care has grown significantly. A Level 1 Trauma Center in the neighborhood would help ensure timely, life-saving treatment for residents and visitors alike.
rows.headline: Other Capital health care facilities request
rows.response: OMB supports the agency's position as follows: Agency does not support and cannot accommodate Explanation: While the cost associated with a Level I Trauma Center is prohibitive at this time due to the requirement of 24/7 trauma surgery and anesthesia coverage, South Brooklyn Health is able to care for hundreds of traumatically injured patients per year in its fully prepared resuscitation rooms. The hospital has a trauma response team on standby for any incoming codes and performs multiple drills to be ready for patients that are brought in for care. In addition, the hospital recently appointed an EMS and Disaster Fellowship trained Director for Trauma and Prehospital Medicine to ensure preparedness and quality. The new 11-story tower building includes a new elevated Emergency Department, state of the art operating rooms including robotic surgery, single bedded inpatient beds, a number of modern specialty care endoscopy and interventional radiology and cardiology services, new entrances from Ocean Parkway, a new flood wall, improved parking for patients and staff, and much more. The redevelopment is part of a major $922.7 million hospital campus renovation funded by the Federal Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) to demolish, replace and repair flood damaged buildings from Superstorm Sandy.
